digest.component_or_area: parent-child status cascade table and lifecycle documentation
propositions: The _CASCADING_EDGES table's one-eligible-status-per-edge shape guarantees only per-edge, same-edge cascades and does not prevent all child advancement relative to parent, leaving two documented-intended residuals reachable.

No non-terminal-state ticket can be a child of a closed ticket; this invariant is maintained jointly by the enumerated cascade table's closed-source rows and the unconditional open-children close guard in transition_close.py.

Reactivating a closed child under an open parent does not cascade because only a closed parent is eligible on that edge; this residual is documented as accepted and pinned by test_reactivate_does_not_disturb_open_parent.

The blocked→in_progress resume does not cascade under an open parent; this is resolved as documented non-cascading despite the start-work gate firing on that transition, because (a) a blocked child cannot sit under a closed ancestor, (b) only a blocked parent would be eligible per the same-edge rule, and (c) the gate and cascade answer different questions.
The §I4a headline must be narrowed from 'A child never runs ahead of its parent' to state only what the enumerated table guarantees, with residuals explicitly documented.
The enumerated _CASCADING_EDGES table is retained; no ordering-predicate redesign is undertaken; table rows remain byte-identical and no permission logic changes.
